objective: Resolve all six TASK-006 review findings with fail-closed guard handling, encoding-safe SessionStart output, and mutation-sensitive UTF-8 tests while preserving the established production file-encoding behavior.
requirements: Make stop_guard.py convert UnicodeDecodeError and relevant filesystem read failures from implementation.md or context.jsonl into exit code 2 with an explanatory stderr diagnostic.
Make session_start.py report unreadable UTF-8 inputs on stderr, omit only the unreadable input, continue with any remaining readable context, and exit 0.
Emit SessionStart context as explicit UTF-8 bytes so output containing Japanese or other non-cp1252 text is preserved even when the stdout text layer is configured for cp1252.

Strengthen the two existing context round-trip tests in place so they exercise non-ASCII bytes rather than json.dumps default ASCII escaping and fail when their required production encoding argument is removed.
Strengthen test_ascii_content_is_byte_for_byte_unchanged in place by comparing produced bytes with an independently constructed deterministic expected artifact, not with a decode/re-encode identity.

Add deterministic mutation tests that remove each targeted encoding argument from an in-memory or temporary source copy and prove the corresponding encoding check fails without depending on the host locale.
Correct binary-mode detection for open(path, 'rb'), os.fdopen(fd, 'rb'), Path.open('rb'), and keyword mode forms while retaining detection of text calls lacking encoding.
Parse each scoped source once per unchanged source value while allowing mutation tests to audit uncached source text.

Preserve valid hook behavior, including allowing a completed write-back, blocking an incomplete write-back, remaining quiet outside an orchestrated task, and continuing SessionStart injection when one optional input is unreadable.

files_to_modify.purpose: Centralize guarded UTF-8 reads and translate expected decode or read failures into an explanatory fail-closed exit code 2.
Add visible read-failure degradation and explicit UTF-8 stdout emission without changing the hook's non-blocking contract.
Strengthen the three ineffective tests, add deterministic source-mutation checks, correct binary-mode classification, and reuse parsed AST results.

files_to_create.purpose: Provide isolated subprocess regressions for malformed hook inputs, exit-code contracts, diagnostics, partial SessionStart degradation, and UTF-8 output through a cp1252-configured text layer.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Malformed UTF-8 in either Stop guard input blocks with exit code 2 and an explanatory stderr reason, while valid and incomplete write-back behavior retains its existing allow/block contract.
SessionStart exits 0 and preserves Japanese text as UTF-8 when its stdout text layer is forced to cp1252, while unreadable inputs are reported and readable remaining context is still emitted.
Each strengthened encoding-specific test has deterministic mutation coverage proving that removal of its required encoding argument is detected, independent of the host filesystem locale.

The AST audit treats positional and keyword binary modes for built-in open, os.fdopen, and Path.open as binary, continues to report text calls without encoding, and reuses parsing only for unchanged source.
The complete repository unittest suite is non-empty and passes under the interpreter executing validation; Python 3.9 and 3.12 coverage is supplied by the existing CI matrix.
acceptance_criteria.verify: {python} -c "import unittest; s=unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover('.'); n=s.countTestCases(); print('discovered %d tests' % n); r=unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(s); raise SystemExit(0 if n > 0 and r.wasSuccessful() else 1)"

constraints: Use only the Python standard library.
A Stop guard failure to read verdict-dependent input must fail closed with exit code 2 and a reason; it must never escape as exit code 1.
SessionStart remains a non-blocking injector: expected input read failures must be visible on stderr but must not return exit code 2.
Do not weaken, delete, or merely relabel the existing F4 and F5 tests; strengthen their assertions in place and retain their test methods as encoding or compatibility regressions.

Keep the explicit UTF-8 file encoding arguments introduced by TASK-006 in .ai/scripts/orchestrator.py, .ai/scripts/review-package.py, .ai/hooks/session_start.py, and .ai/hooks/stop_guard.py exactly as established.
Do not change json.dumps production behavior, newline translation, _support.py text I/O, diff-scope base selection, or unrelated attribute-call classification.
Maintain compatibility with Python 3.9 and Python 3.12; the existing .github/workflows/ci.yml matrix owns multi-version execution and must not be modified.
Acceptance commands may invoke only the orchestrator-provided {python} interpreter and must reject an empty suite.
Workflow hook changes are explicitly declared as required by the constitution and ADR-0004.
Do not modify task evidence or orchestrator-owned verdict artifacts.
risks: The previous plan's production architecture was broadly sound, but its validation contract was not: AC-3 did not prove the formerly tautological tests fail under mutation, and AC-5 used inaccessible interpreter launchers while allowing an empty suite.

Writing to sys.stdout.buffer bypasses locale encoding as required, but test harnesses may replace stdout with a text-only object; any fallback must preserve content or fail visibly rather than silently replacing non-ASCII text.
Catching exceptions too broadly could hide programming defects, so hook handling should be limited to expected UnicodeDecodeError and filesystem read failures.

A SessionStart implementation that returns immediately after one unreadable input could still lose readable constitution or blackboard content; tests must cover partial degradation in both directions.

Mutation tests can become false confidence if they mutate a call unrelated to the assertion; each mutant must target a uniquely identified production call and assert that the intended check changes from pass to fail.
Path-only AST caching can return stale results after controlled mutation; cache keys must incorporate source identity or mutation audits must use an uncached source-level helper.

Scanning all string positional arguments for binary modes is adequate for the supported APIs but could misclassify an unrelated method call; this task intentionally does not broaden the existing TEXT_IO_NAMES receiver model.

The repository currently contains overlapping uncommitted TASK-006/TASK-007 work; implementation must preserve unrelated changes and validation scope remains dependent on the orchestrator resolving its separately acknowledged diff-base issue.
test_strategy: Run stop_guard.py from temporary repository-shaped directories with malformed implementation.md and context.jsonl bytes, asserting exit 2, useful stderr, no traceback-only exit 1, and unchanged valid/incomplete write-back behavior.

Run session_start.py as a subprocess with Japanese context and a deliberately cp1252-configured stdout text layer, capture raw stdout bytes, and assert exact UTF-8 content and exit 0 on every supported host.
Test unreadable constitution and blackboard inputs independently, asserting a diagnostic and continued emission of whichever source remains readable.
Make context serialization tests emit real non-ASCII file content within the test fixture so their byte assertions cannot be satisfied solely by ensure_ascii=True escaping.
Make the ASCII compatibility test deterministic by fixing dynamic block fields and comparing the entire produced JSONL byte sequence with an independently constructed expected ASCII sequence.

For every encoding-specific regression, remove the uniquely targeted encoding keyword from source in memory or a temporary copy, use an instrumented default text opener where necessary to avoid host-locale dependence, and assert the associated check fails.
Exercise AST helpers directly with built-in open, os.fdopen, Path.open, keyword binary mode, text-mode counterexamples, os.open exclusion, cache reuse, and uncached mutated source.

Run the focused hook and UTF-8 test classes first, then the guarded non-empty full-suite command under the current validation interpreter; rely on the unchanged CI matrix for Python 3.9 and 3.12 coverage.
